meta.title: BackToHealth · Live better with back pain
meta.description: A mobile app for chronic low back pain: a little movement, reading, meditation and walking, each day, following what your back tells you.

hero.label: Mobile app · iPhone and Android
hero.title: Live better with back pain, one small step at a time.
hero.body: Each day, a little movement, a short read, a moment for the mind and some walking. BackToHealth follows what your back tells you.
hero.phoneAlt: The BackToHealth app on a phone: the tree on the hill and today’s program

who.label: Who it’s for
who.title: Your back has hurt for months. Maybe years.
who.body: You’ve heard a lot and tried a lot. Mostly, you’d like to get back to what matters: gardening, carrying your kids, driving without thinking about your back.
who.fact: You are far from alone: about 9 times out of 10, back pain has no specific cause that can be identified.
for: You’re an adult, and your back pain has lasted several months.
No serious cause explains your back pain: this is called non-specific low back pain.
You want to move forward at your own pace, without pressure.

water.label: How it works
water.title: Every effort waters your tree.
water.body: You begin with an assessment of about 5 minutes, then choose your rhythm. Each finished activity becomes a drop of water.
water.end: Your tree grows with the days you took care of yourself, not with a streak to keep. It never wilts.

steps.label: Learn
steps.title: Understand your back pain
steps.body: About 5 minutes of reading. 23 short lessons, written by our doctor, who also holds a degree in physiotherapy, to understand what’s going on and regain confidence.

steps.label: Movement
steps.title: Move, at your measure
steps.body: 5 to 15 minutes, 2 or 3 times a week. Exercises are chosen from your assessment and demonstrated with 3D animations.

steps.label: Mind
steps.title: A moment to breathe
steps.body: Mindfulness, from 3 to 30 minutes, for when the day or your back pain feels heavy.

steps.label: Walking
steps.title: Go for a walk
steps.body: As far as you like. And if you did yoga or went cycling elsewhere, that counts too: you can log it.

pain.label: An app that listens
pain.title: If your back pain rises, we ease off.
pain.body: During exercises, you say where your back pain is, and the program follows. Try it: imagine you just finished a set.
pain.easyBody: We move forward gently: if your whole session goes like this, you’ll do one more repetition next time.
pain.holdBody: You can carry on. Next time, we keep the same level.
pain.stopBody: Stop this exercise, it’s the right call. Next time, we start again a little more gently. If you like, a 3-minute comfort moment is waiting for you.

screens.label: In the app
screens.title: One thing at a time.
screens.s1Body: A short program. Nothing to catch up on.
screens.s2Body: Lessons, one at a time, across the landscape.
screens.s3Body: You choose how much time you have.
screens.s4Body: What is getting easier, in your own words.

pros.label: Health professionals
pros.title: Support between your appointments, and after them.
pros.body: BackToHealth replaces neither your assessment nor your follow-up. It helps your patients with chronic low back pain keep moving, understanding and looking after themselves, especially once their sessions end.
pros.ctaTitle: Would you like to try it or tell us what you think?
pros.ctaBody: We’re looking for clinicians to review the content and offer the app to their patients.

cards.title: Screening comes first
cards.body: 8 red-flag questions before any program. A positive answer directs the person to a doctor or the ER.

cards.title: A clear rule for low back pain
cards.body: Above 3/10: stop and step down a level. A full session at 2/10 or less: one more repetition, up to 12, then the next level.

cards.title: A biopsychosocial approach
cards.body: Exercise, low back pain education, mindfulness and walking in one program, as practice guidelines recommend.

cards.title: What we don’t claim
cards.body: The app does not diagnose or treat. It has not yet been the subject of a published study. With people’s consent, we will measure what works.

team.label: Who we are
team.title: A team of committed innovators, in Montréal.
team.body: BackToHealth builds on recent research on chronic back pain. Behind the app are three people who put their energy into it.

people.name: Pierre-Henri Bao Heitz
people.title: Project founder
people.bio: Physician, also trained in physiotherapy, with expertise in recent research on chronic back pain. He created the clinical content, validates it and leads the project.

people.name: Adrien Moevus
people.title: App lead
people.bio: Medical student and full-stack developer. He designs the service’s architecture and builds the app end to end. He also writes the meditations.

people.name: Antoine Moevus
people.title: Business and development
people.bio: He leads business and development, and is responsible for data and AI governance, including the use of machine learning in the app.

items.q: Does it replace my doctor or physio?
items.a: No. BackToHealth helps you live better with back pain, alongside your care. If something worries you, talk to a health professional.

items.q: What if it hurts too much, or I don’t feel like it, on a given day?
items.a: Every activity has a “Not today” button that offers something gentler. During a flare-up, the plan lightens for 3 days. Your tree waits for you, no rush.

items.q: When does the app come out?
items.a: We’re testing it now, on iPhone and Android. Write to us to hear when it launches.
The price isn’t set yet. We’ll tell you clearly before launch.
In French and English. It follows your phone’s language, and you can change it whenever you like.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: This information touches on your health: we protect it, we never sell it, and you can export or delete it at any time. Using it for research is optional, and happens under a code, never with your name or email.

end.title: Your tree is waiting.
end.body: Send us a note: we’ll tell you when you can plant it.

footer.disclaimer: BackToHealth helps you live better with back pain. The app does not replace the advice of a health professional.

offer.label: The program
offer.title: To start, four introductory programs.
offer.body: These are your first steps. For a few weeks, the app teaches you to understand your back, to move, to meditate and to walk. Then it stays with you for as long as you like.
offer.goalTitle: And after? We stay with you.
offer.goalBody: Once the introductions are done, you keep your tools: your exercises keep adapting to your pain, you meditate your own way, you keep your walking rhythm, and you redo your tests to see how far you’ve come. And if you want to go further, a Pilates, yoga or meditation class is even better.

cards.body: 23 five-minute lessons, about one a day, to understand your back pain and regain confidence.
Progressive exercises, chosen from your assessment and adapted to your pain, 2 to 3 times a week.
A mindfulness program, then two paths: kindness toward yourself, and what matters to you.
A progressive walking program, with a weekly goal that starts from what you already do.

meta.title: The program in detail · BackToHealth
meta.description: The exercises and their dosing, the 23 lessons, the meditation program and walking in the BackToHealth app, for patients and health professionals.

program.label: The program in detail
program.title: What BackToHealth contains, step by step.
program.lead: For curious people and health professionals: the assessment, exercises, lessons, meditation and walking, as they are in the app.
program.status: The clinical content is being validated by our doctor, who also holds a degree in physiotherapy. It may still change.
g3: 10 to 30 min, or 3 min of comfort
g4: 8 weeks, then at your own pace
program.evalTitle: First: an assessment of about 5 minutes
eval: 8 red-flag questions. A positive answer points the person to a doctor or the ER, and the program doesn’t start.
4 movement tests: flexion, extension, rotation to the right and to the left, with the pain during each. They set the starting exercises and their level.
1 to 3 activities the person wants to get back to, rated from 0 to 10 (Patient-Specific Functional Scale).
The rhythm: a little every day, some light days and some more active ones, or a few chosen days a week.
program.familiesTitle: The exercises, from easiest to most demanding
program.medDaily: Between sessions, the idea is to return to that state for a few moments in the day, 30 seconds to 2 minutes, without effort.
follow: The activities chosen at the start are re-rated about every 2 weeks.
The movement tests are repeated about every 4 weeks, to compare before and now.
Pain is tracked over time, and a weekly summary shows what was done.
During a flare-up, the plan lightens for 3 days: no exercise session, comfort moments and gentle walking.
The person can export their data at any time.
program.philoTitle: A toolbox, not a takeover of care
program.philoBody: BackToHealth gives the tools and the first steps on each path. The program is enough on its own, and going further elsewhere (a Pilates class, a meditation workshop, follow-up in a clinic) is even better. The person stays in charge of their path.
program.glanceNote: These are the lengths of the introductory programs. The app then continues, with no time limit.
after: Exercises keep adapting to pain, and new exercises are offered when a level becomes easy.
Meditation continues with the practice the person has built, from 10 to 30 minutes.
Walking keeps its rhythm, or aims a little higher, up to about 2 hours a week.
Lessons stay available to reread, and the movement tests can be redone to compare.
Going further elsewhere (Pilates, yoga, meditation, clinic follow-up) is encouraged.
program.exIdea: Moving without fear, guided by pain. The starting exercises are chosen from the movement tests. They cover extension, flexion, rotation and trunk stabilisation, then strength (upper body, squat, lunge, hips). Pain up to 3/10 is acceptable: it doesn’t mean damage.
program.exProgress: 3 sets of 10 to 12 repetitions. A session done at 2/10 or less adds a repetition; at 12, the next level. Above 3/10, the exercise stops and goes down a level. When a family’s top level becomes easy, the app offers a more demanding exercise from another family.
program.exExample: Glute bridge: 3 × 10, then 3 × 11, then 3 × 12, then Bird-dog at 3 × 10.
program.eduIdea: Understanding chronic pain to regain confidence: the pain is real, but it doesn’t mean the back is damaged. Then a healthy lifestyle, pain management techniques, and an acceptance and commitment approach.
program.eduProgress: One lesson of about 5 minutes per active day, in order, with a question at each step.
program.medIdea: Learning to live with back pain rather than making it disappear. Secular mindfulness, trained in sessions and then used during the day.
program.medProgress: A first guided session for each practice, then free sessions with short reminders. 10 minutes in week 1, 15 after, and up to 30 if the person wants.
medThemes: The breath, and coming back when the mind wanders
The body scan, from head to feet
Kindness: talking to yourself as to a friend
What matters: stopping the struggle, thoughts as clouds, your values
program.walkIdea: Getting back into the habit of walking, at your own pace. A goal in minutes per week, never per day: a bad day can be made up later, or not at all.
program.walkProgress: The program starts from what the person already walks (at least 15 minutes a week) and aims for about double in 8 weeks, between 45 and 125 minutes, about 10 % more each week. If pain goes above 3/10, the goal stays the same; two weeks in a row, the person walks as much as they can without going above 3/10, and the plan restarts from there.
program.walkExample: Starting at 30 minutes a week: 30, 33, 37, 40, 45, 49, 54, then 60 minutes.
